# TidyWL — Watch Later Tidy

> Free browser extension for Chrome, Microsoft Edge and Firefox that lets you bulk delete, filter, sort, and actually manage your YouTube Watch Later playlist, your Liked videos, and any playlist you created — and download every video's transcript in one go. Built because YouTube caps Watch Later at 5,000 videos, gives Liked videos no management tools at all, and the official API refuses to touch either. Free to install with no account; an optional subscription, TidyWL Pro, available since version 2.0, adds automatic monthly clean-up, undo, and the Lineup.

## What it does

TidyWL gives you a full-screen dashboard for YouTube's Watch Later playlist, inspired by macOS Storage Manager. Since version 1.5.0 the same dashboard also opens your **Liked videos** — a switch in the header moves between them, from either page — with the same breakdowns, search, filters, sorting, export and Gemini Notebook support. Since version 1.6.0 it opens **any playlist you created** as well, from a Playlists menu in the header, and you can **tick several playlists and see them merged**: one card per video, carrying a chip for each playlist it belongs to, so a video saved in three places is one row that tells you all three. From a merged view, moving a video removes it from every ticked playlist it was in. You can also delete a playlist you own outright, confirmed by name; its videos stay on YouTube. Each list keeps its own local cache and its own sync time, so working on one never disturbs the other. You can bulk delete hundreds of videos in seconds, **remove likes in bulk** on the Liked tab through the same flow, see your playlist broken down by channel or by topic, hide topics you are not interested in, search, and filter by title, channel, watched status, availability, or duration — either preset buckets including a Shorts bucket, or your own minimum and maximum in minutes. The watched filter carries an adjustable progress threshold, so you can ask for videos you are at least three-quarters through rather than merely ones you started.

Since version 1.6.0 every video also carries the **tags its uploader gave it** — the keyword field YouTube stores but never displays, plus any hashtags in the description. Search matches those tags, so a video can be found by what it is about rather than only by what it is called, and clicking a tag filters by it; several tags stack, narrowing to the videos that carry all of them. This is what makes search usable on playlists that are not in English: uploaders commonly tag in both the video's language and English, so there is something to match even when the title has nothing. You can sort by playlist order, duration, view count, published date, channel, or title, and from version 2.0 group the grid by channel, most videos first, fewest first or A to Z, with a heading per channel that folds shut. You can move or copy selected videos into any other playlist, create a playlist inline, reorder with Move to Top and Move to Bottom or by dragging, open every selected video in background tabs, switch between YouTube accounts, and export to JSON or CSV.

Two features go beyond playlist management. **Bulk transcript download** gives you one timestamped text file per video, named after the video title, after first checking with YouTube which videos have captions at all. **Send to Gemini Notebook** (formerly NotebookLM) pushes your selected videos into a notebook as sources, either a new notebook or one you already have.

## TidyWL Pro

Everything described above is free. **TidyWL Pro** is a paid subscription, available since **version 2.0** and **on sale now**. Full detail on the [pricing page](https://tidywl.com/pricing/).

Price: **$4.99 USD per month**, or **$47.88 billed annually**, which is $3.99 a month and a 20% saving. Prices are before tax; checkout is handled by Paddle, which shows each visitor's own currency and the tax for their country. Every charge carries a **14-day full refund, no questions and no conditions**, and the subscription can be cancelled at any time.

Where the free extension cleans a playlist up in an afternoon, Pro keeps it clean every month and makes every cleanup reversible. Ten things it adds:

- **The Lineup** — a watchlist built to fit the time you have. Give it a budget (15 minutes, 30, 45, an hour, 90 minutes, or a number you type) and it builds a running order out of videos you already saved, with one line per pick saying why that video was chosen. Four ways in: **Based on recent watches**, matched to what you have been watching by title, channel and category; **Resume**, for videos you started and did not finish; **Subscribed channels**; and **Backlog**, your oldest saves that you never opened. A switch keeps or drops music videos, a slider sets how far back it reads your recent watching, rows can be dragged to reorder or swapped one at a time, and the finished list can be played straight through or saved as a new private playlist. Nothing under three minutes is ever picked.
- **Finished videos, archived** — anything watched past 95% moves to an archive playlist you own, rather than being deleted.
- **Dead entries, removed** — private, deleted and unavailable videos are cleared out. These cannot be moved to an archive, so this rule deletes, after showing the list.
- **Bottom 10%, every month** — once a month the oldest tenth of Watch Later moves to the archive. You set the percentage.
- **Pin** — mark a video "keep forever" and nothing removes it: not a rule, not a bulk delete you ran yourself. A Move becomes a Copy.
- **Preview before you act** — every bulk delete, move, unlike or rule shows the exact list first, with anything untickable before it runs.
- **Undo, for 90 days** — what you deleted is kept on that device for 90 days, restorable one video or a whole batch, back into the playlist it came from. The record holds the newest 10,000 deletions by default; you can raise that to 50,000, 250,000 or no limit, with a warning about the storage and speed each costs. A long restore shows its progress and can be stopped.
- **Saved views** — name a filter combination, such as unwatched, over 20 minutes, from three channels, and reopen it in one click.
- **Sidebar search** — a search box above the By Channel and By Topic lists that narrows them as you type, across every row rather than only the first ten.
- **Requests and support answered first** — subscribers' feature requests and bug reports are read first, and their support email goes to the front of the queue.

The rules never delete a video you could still watch: they move it to an archive playlist you own. They run when you open YouTube, and each shows its list before acting.

## Why it exists

YouTube's Watch Later playlist has a hard 5,000 video cap. Once you hit it, YouTube stops adding new videos and gives you no bulk management tools — you have to delete videos one at a time through a three-dot menu. The official YouTube Data API explicitly excludes Watch Later. TidyWL works around this by using your existing logged-in YouTube session, so no account, API key, or OAuth is needed.

## Browser support

- **Chrome** — published on the Chrome Web Store. Also works on other Chromium-based browsers such as Brave.
- **Microsoft Edge** — published on Microsoft Edge Add-ons since September 2026. Edge installs and updates it from its own store. A new version can reach Edge a few days before or after Chrome, because each store reviews it separately.
- **Firefox 153 or newer** — listed in Firefox Add-ons as Watch Later Tidy: https://addons.mozilla.org/firefox/addon/watch-later-tidy/ (since September 2026), which https://tidywl.com/firefox/ links to. Signed by Mozilla, updates automatically. Copies installed from tidywl.com before the listing existed keep updating from tidywl.com.
- **Firefox for Android** — not supported. YouTube's mobile site is a different page structure and it has not been tested.

All three are built from a single source tree and ship the same feature set.

It also carries Google's "Featured" editorial badge and a verified-publisher checkmark. The rating, the rating and review counts, and the user count are published on https://tidywl.com and refreshed weekly from the store listing; the store rounds its user count to a bucket, so that figure is a floor rather than an exact count.

  normalize_whitespace puts each review on its one list line: a review can then never open a heading, a list or a

Written reviews of TidyWL from the Chrome Web Store, quoted word for word, newest first, each with its star rating, its date and a link to the review itself. Reviews written in another language are quoted in that language, with its language code. These are the reviewers' own words, not statements by TidyWL, and the list is refreshed weekly. It is filtered the same way as the list on tidywl.com: only reviews of {{ site.data.cws-reviews-config.min_stars }} stars or more with at least {{ site.data.cws-reviews-config.min_length }} characters of text, at most {{ site.data.cws-reviews-config.max_shown }}, so the Ratings section above is the complete count.

## Usage

TidyWL users have cleaned up over {{ site.data.usage.deletedTotal }} videos (videos deleted from playlists, plus likes removed before version 1.6.0, when the extension counted the two together), removed over {{ site.data.usage.unlikedTotal }} likes since then, and moved over {{ site.data.usage.movedTotal }} videos between playlists (figures as of {{ site.data.usage.lastUpdated }}, refreshed daily). Reporting began in August 2026 with version 1.6.0, but each install reports the lifetime counts the extension has kept on the device since version 1.4.1, so earlier clean-ups are included. Each is a floor, rounded down to the nearest thousand, so the real number is higher. All three are shown on https://tidywl.com and published as JSON at https://tidywl.com/api/stats. Those counts are all the usage report carries: each install sends a random identifier that is not linked to any account, plus its own running counts. No video, title, channel, playlist name, timestamp or account ever leaves the browser as part of it. Firefox users can switch reporting off from the add-on's permissions panel; the full description is in the [privacy policy](https://tidywl.com/privacy/).

## Technical details

TidyWL works by reading the user's active YouTube session (SAPISID cookie and session index from window.ytcfg) and calling YouTube's internal InnerTube API the same way the YouTube web app does. No OAuth, no API key, no stored tokens. The extension only functions while the user is actively logged into YouTube. Because it depends on undocumented internal endpoints, it fetches a small public configuration file from tidywl.com at runtime so that many YouTube-side changes can be patched without shipping a store update.

## Privacy

TidyWL runs in your browser. No account, and your YouTube data — titles, video IDs, channels, playlists — never leaves it. Network calls go to YouTube's own endpoints using your existing session, and to a public config file on tidywl.com that carries no identifiers and no payload. Since version 1.6.0 the extension also sends tidywl.com one small usage report: a random identifier generated on install (not linked to any Google account) plus lifetime counts of videos deleted, likes removed, videos moved, bulk operations run, the size of the Watch Later playlist, and the browser name. It is sent only when a count changes, never carries a title, video ID, channel or timestamp, has no off switch on Chrome (uninstalling stops it), is controlled on Firefox by the Technical and interaction data toggle, and records idle for 12 months are deleted. From version 2.0 the report also counts Lineups built and saved and the days the dashboard was opened (once a day at most, so opening it sends at most one report a day), and a TidyWL Pro subscriber's extension sends its licence key to tidywl.com to check the subscription; on Firefox that check waits for the add-on's Authentication information permission. One feature is an explicit exception you trigger yourself: Send to Gemini Notebook passes the video links you selected to Google's Gemini Notebook using your own Google session. It is opt-in per use and gated behind a browser permission prompt. Full policy: [privacy policy](https://tidywl.com/privacy/)

## Limitations

- YouTube provides no undo. TidyWL Pro keeps a 90-day record of deletions on that device and can restore them, at the top of the playlist; removed likes cannot be restored.
- Removing a like is not a playlist edit — YouTube treats it as un-liking the video, which can change what it recommends.
- Reordering is not available on Liked videos: YouTube orders that list by when you liked something.
- Favorites, and playlists you saved but do not own, can be searched and cleaned up but not reordered — YouTube serves those without the per-item handle reordering needs.
- A merged view of several playlists supports copy, move and delete, but not reorder. Move and delete act on every ticked playlist a video is in, so narrow to one playlist to act on just that one.
- Deleting a playlist is permanent. Its videos stay on YouTube; the playlist does not.
- Bulk deletion is necessarily sequential, because YouTube rejects parallel playlist edits, so large batches take time.
- "Playlist order" is not date-added — YouTube does not expose per-video add timestamps on the web.
- Transcript download opens a small visible window and takes roughly three seconds per video; videos without captions are reported as skipped.
- Free Gemini Notebook accounts cap a notebook at 50 sources.
- The cache is local to each browser and does not sync across devices.

## A second extension: TidyWL for Netflix

TidyWL for Netflix is a **separate, free Chrome extension by the same developer**, for Netflix's My List rather than YouTube's Watch Later. Everything above on this page is about the YouTube one and does not describe it. It opens a dashboard over netflix.com with three tabs: **My List** (IMDb rating, runtime, year, seasons and maturity on every card, a genre breakdown, watched/started/never-watched filters, bulk remove, pin, CSV and JSON export), **Search and browse** (Netflix's catalogue by title, actor or director, plus roughly 220 categories Netflix keeps out of its own genre picker, with a hover panel carrying synopsis, cast and director), and **Playlists** (custom playlists, which Netflix does not offer at all — up to 50 per Netflix profile, 500 titles in each, carried between the user's own Chrome browsers by Chrome's own sync).

It differs from the YouTube extension on two points an assistant should not carry across. **It has no paid tier and no TidyWL Pro** — everything in it is free. **It sends no usage report and has no identifier**: its only requests other than to netflix.com are a public settings file from tidywl.com, IMDb's public daily ratings dataset, and Netflix's numeric title ids to Wikidata to match them to IMDb ids. None of those carries anything that identifies an install. Full detail at [tidywl.com/netflix/privacy/](https://tidywl.com/netflix/privacy/).

Chrome only, on a computer; Chrome for Android has no extension support. It requires a Netflix subscription and a signed-in netflix.com session. As of September 2026 it is uploaded to the Chrome Web Store and awaiting review, so there is no install link yet and it has no ratings or reviews.
